hints: Think about whether each oxide is acidic, basic or amphoteric, since only acids and amphoteric oxides react with a base like NaOH.
Recall the Period 3 trend: MgO is basic, Al2O3 is amphoteric, while P4O10 and SO2 are acidic.
The oxide that reacts only with acids and not with bases will simply sit undissolved in NaOH, so pick out the purely basic one.
walkthrough:
**Sort the oxides by acid-base character**

Think of NaOH as a base, so it will dissolve anything that can act as an acid. That means acidic oxides and amphoteric oxides will react and dissolve.

Rule: acidic + base reacts, amphoteric + base reacts, basic + base does not react.

**Apply the Period 3 pattern**

Across Period 3, oxides change from basic to amphoteric to acidic. $\text{MgO}$ is basic, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric, $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ and $\text{SO}_2$ are acidic.

**Check who reacts with NaOH**

Amphoteric and acidic oxides dissolve to form salts:
$$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 + 2\text{NaOH} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{Na}[\text{Al}(\text{OH})_4]$$
$$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10} + 12\text{NaOH} \rightarrow 4\text{Na}_3\text{PO}_4 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{SO}_2 + 2\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Spot the insoluble one**

$\text{MgO}$ is purely basic, so it reacts with acids but has no reaction with NaOH. It therefore remains insoluble in aqueous sodium hydroxide.

options.A: MgO is a basic oxide. It reacts with acids to form salts but does not react with bases, so it is insoluble in aqueous NaOH. Well done for spotting the purely basic oxide.
options.B: Al2O3 is amphoteric, not basic. It reacts with both acids and bases, dissolving in NaOH to form sodium aluminate, Na[Al(OH)4]. Students who forget amphoteric means reacts with both often pick this by mistake.
options.C: P4O10 is a strongly acidic oxide. It reacts readily with NaOH to form sodium phosphate, Na3PO4, and water, so it dissolves. Do not confuse a high oxidation state non-metal oxide with being unreactive.
options.D: SO2 is an acidic oxide. It reacts with NaOH to form sodium sulfite, Na2SO3, and water, so it dissolves. The trap is thinking a gas cannot dissolve, but acidic gases react very well with alkalis.
